subject: QBR: infra heatmap + cost-sensitivity asks (GPU spend / batching impact)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: QBR: infra heatmap + cost-sensitivity asks (GPU spend / batching impact)

Team —

QBR is two weeks out and leadership wants a concise infra appendix focused on three things: GPU spend & utilization, sensitivity to batching/caching changes, and a short list of conservative cost levers we can pull during the quarter. Key constraints: keep the appendix to 2 slides and one backup spreadsheet with scenarios.

Ask list (high priority):
- Rishi: produce a 3-tier heatmap (worst/likely/best) for GPU utilization across Hosted / Dedicated / Private for next 90 days. Include assumptions for traffic and on-call rate.
- Marcus: run cost-sensitivity sims for +/-20% batching and +/-15% cache hit. Show net $/generated-token impact and an elasticity estimate.
- Vivek: prepare recommended emergency levers (e.g., autoscale floor changes, instance-family switches, temporary quantization toggles) and the operational risk for each.

Deliverables timeline: initial drafts by EOD Tue (4/19), final slide + workbook by EOD Thu (4/21). Lauren — can you own the final slide narrative and the single-slide exec summary?

Notes: leadership will ask for an example customer impact (call out any high-spend customers). I cc'd Lauren so she can add executive framing. If anybody needs data pulls (billing, GPU telemetry), ping infra-observability; I can escalate.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr-infra-heatmap-20270418.xlsx (workbook stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: infra heatmap + cost-sensitivity asks (GPU spend / batching impact)

Jonas — thanks, starting this now. Quick status and questions:

1) Heatmap: I pulled last 12 weeks of telemetry from the serving runtime and normalized by seq length 128/512 buckets. First-pass notes attached (sheet tab: raw-telemetry). Early signal: Hosted shows the highest amplitude variance (spiky freescaling traffic) while Dedicated has more stable but lower headroom.

2) Assumptions: for the 'likely' case I'm using current forecasted qps + 8% weekly growth; for worst I apply an additional 25% weekend spike assumption. Need confirmation if we should include a planned feature rollout on May 1 (customer-facing summarization) — that would add ~6-9% token volume in our model.

3) Data ask: Marcus — I will hand you the per-model token mix CSV in the sheet (tab: per_model_mix) so your cost sims can apply correct token weighting.

I'll have the heatmap workbook (first-pass) attached by EOD today. If you want a quick sync I can do a 20-min call at 2pm.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr-infra-heatmap-20270418.xlsx (heatmap workbook, tab: raw-telemetry)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: infra heatmap + cost-sensitivity asks (GPU spend / batching impact)

Rishi / Jonas — attaching a short sim summary (batching-sim-results-3p.pdf) and a few callouts below. I used the per_model_mix from Rishi and baseline prices from our April invoice (projected).

Top-line:
- Batching elasticity: increasing effective batch sizes by 20% (through config + smarter routing) yields ~12.4% reduction in $/token in the Hosted pool, ~9.1% in Dedicated. Gains taper after ~30% because of latency guardrails.
- Cache hit sensitivity: improving KV/prefix cache hit by 15% produces a ~7.6% $/token improvement on average; impact concentrated on long-tail LLM requests.
- Combined scenario (batch +15%, cache +10%): ~18.3% unit cost improvement but increases tail-latency exposure — see risk table.

Operational notes:
- The biggest single-dollar lever short-term is routing more stable traffic (higher-entropy workloads) to Dedicated where batching is more efficient; estimated quarterly savings if we shift 10% of Hosted steady traffic: ~$320k.
- Quantization toggles help but introduce output-quality risk; modeled as possible only for internal/non-PII inference for now.

I've put detailed sims in the PDF and flagged assumptions. Rishi — I used your worst/likely/best heatmap as the traffic envelope. Vivek — would like your risk gradings for each lever in the final.

Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: batching-sim-results-3p.pdf (summary + per-scenario tables)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Dunn <michael.dunn@acme.com>, aws-partner@cloudmarket.com
Date: 2027-04-20T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: infra heatmap + cost-sensitivity asks (GPU spend / batching impact)

Thanks for the quick turn. I reviewed both attachments and pulled the top-line for the exec slide. Draft narrative below — please flag any factual errors by EOD tomorrow. I'll convert to a single-slide executive summary after sign-off.

Draft exec narrative (short):
- Context: Finalize QBR infra appendix showing realistic spend envelopes and three prioritized levers to reduce unit cost without materially affecting customer SLAs.
- Findings: Combined batching and caching improvements could reduce $/token by ~18% in the mid-case; shifting steady traffic to Dedicated yields the largest immediate dollar savings (~$320k/quarter).
- Ask from leadership: approval to run a 2-week pilot to increase batching floor by 12% in Hosted for low-risk model groups and to enable dynamic routing rules for steady long-running queries.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Rishi: finalize heatmap workbook with the May 1 rollout scenario included. (due: EOD Wed 4/21)
- Marcus: finalize sensitivity table and include a short note on latency tradeoffs (due: EOD Wed 4/21)
- Vivek: annotate operational risk for each lever and produce a one-paragraph rollback plan (due: EOD Thu 4/22)
- Jonas/Me: consolidate into 1 slide and a backup workbook; I will also prepare the procurement ask if we need a short-term reserved instance commit.

Michael (external) — tagging you: if Acme wants to consider a short-term committed pool for high-throughput nightly jobs, we should discuss sizing this in the pilot window.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
